analysis.title: Here Come The Banks: Q3 Earnings Preview, Where Positioning Is Most Stretched, Key Focus Topics And Everything You Need To Know
key_insights: S&P 500 consensus Q3 expectations are 12.4% revenue growth, 29.6% earnings growth and 15.0% margins, versus Q2 at 15.6% revenue growth, 52.3% earnings growth and 17% margins. Q4 is expected at 12.4% revenue and 28.0% earnings growth.
FY26 consensus is 12.5% revenue and 32.7% EPS growth. FY27 consensus is 9.4% revenue and 15.8% EPS growth.
JPMorgan notes 11 of 11 sectors are expected to show positive revenue and earnings growth in Q3. This would be the second time in history, after 2021 Q2.

Earnings growth is highly concentrated. AI infrastructure stocks are expected to drive more than half of S&P 500 EPS growth in Q3, and the top 10 contributors account for 68% of Q3 growth, up from 47% in Q1 and 48% in Q2.

Micron contributes 19% of Q3 index EPS growth and Nvidia 15%, together 34%. Then Meta (7%), Alphabet (6%), Broadcom (5%), followed by Exxon, Chevron, Marathon Petroleum (oil shock from the Iran war) and Boeing.

Micron reported year/year earnings growth of 1,003% two weeks ago, beat consensus EPS and gave guidance described as good but slightly light. The stock has fallen since, which the author reads as good news being priced in.
The median S&P 500 stock is expected to grow EPS 9% in Q3, down from 14% in Q2. Analysts project sequential deceleration in every sector except Info Tech and Comm Services.
Analysts have cut the median stock's Q3 profit margin estimate by 11bp since the start of the quarter, with estimates trimmed in every sector except Info Tech.

Goldman: the market is 2% from its all-time high while the median stock is 17% below its high. S&P 500 breadth is at its lowest since the Dot Com Bubble. The median stock was 16% underwater last week per the TMT desk.
JPM watch item (i) breadth: Bloomberg flags 57% of the SPX is in a bear market (down 20%+ from highs), coinciding with declining dispersion. A Tech stumble could trigger a correction.
JPM watch item (ii): in 4 of the last 6 reporting periods the 1-day reaction to beats came in below historical median levels, and misses were punished more than historically.

JPM watch item (iii) capex: the consensus way the AI boom ends is a hyperscaler capex cut. JPM considers this highly unlikely in 2026 earnings, but the market will look for clues including reduced shareholder distributions.

JPM watch item (iv) inflation: the Consumer sector is trading as if in recession, with consumer confidence at all-time lows. DAL has cut profit guidance on energy prices and unwillingness to pass on costs.

Goldman bank EPS focus areas: capital markets normalization after a strong 2Q26, NII given the sharp rise in rates and more hawkish forward curve, deposit costs, loan growth durability, expenses, capital deployment (possible buyback pauses at regionals like USB), credit (reserve releases possible, watch multifamily CRE), consumer health, and agentic AI.

Single-name questions: BAC NII upside and trading versus peers. WFC near-term NIM and FY26 NII versus $50bn target. JPM 2027 operating leverage. C front-loaded 2H26 investments. KEY whether a 3.25% NIM is achievable. HBAN whether estimates are derisked after the September guidance reset. SCHW rate tailwinds to NII versus balance sheet changes.

Buyside sentiment: large banks mixed, trust banks positive, regionals down from early-summer highs with tactical hedge fund buying, consumer finance notably negative, payments warm, exchanges favored, boutique investment banks among the lowest, mortgage originators negative, life insurers seeing rising long interest.

Hedge fund exposure to US Financials rebounded from the start of last earnings season and is near 3-year averages. US bank L/S ratio fell sharply across large caps and regionals, consumer finance L/S is near 2-year lows, and insurance L/S inflected higher QoQ.

Financials closed lower on 16 of 21 trading sessions in September, tied for the worst month since November 1999. Financials enter earnings after sharply underperforming the S&P 500, and Q4 has historically been favorable seasonally for the sector.

Earnings-reaction history: JPM best reaction in 2 of last 16 quarters and worst in 1. MS best in 5 of 16 and higher in 9 of last 10 prints. WFC lower on 9 of last 13 prints but averaged +5.5% when higher. USB lower after 9 of 12. COF lower 3 straight quarters. AXP lower in 12 of 16 but averaged +7.85% on its 4 up prints. BLK rallied after 7 of 8 prints, averaging +4.3%.

market_movers.rationale: Goldman has WFC on its Conviction List. It sees top-line growth in NII and fees, operating leverage from modest expense growth, and expects WFC to hit its $50bn 2026 NII target as balance sheet growth and repricing outweigh higher deposit costs.

Goldman sees the high end of 2026 NII guidance as achievable. It projects 2027E NII growth of about 7.5% YoY, about 0.5pp above the large-bank average and about 1% above consensus, helped by asset sensitivity and less capital markets risk.
Goldman projects ROTCE of about 11.5% in 2026E and 13.2% in 2028E, with a 4% 2026E-28E core revenue CAGR and efficiency gains. Citi has beaten EPS in all but 4 quarters over the past decade.

sector_views.rationale: Buyside sentiment is mixed, weighing near-term softness versus 2Q against the longer-term pipeline. The sector has often been a source of funds for money leaving Financials or rotating to nonbanks.
Positioning is down from early-summer highs. Hedge funds have bought since the mid-quarter conference on near-term upside to 4Q numbers, but the buying looks tactical and 2027 is still debated.
Sentiment is notably negative among hedge funds and long-only investors, who expect macro conditions and oil tail risk to keep valuation multiples contained.
Sentiment is warm. The group is increasingly viewed as insulated from agentic AI, and spend trends improved into the end of 3Q.
Specialist positioning is among the lowest. Near-term numbers are falling on a 3Q activity air pocket, and boutiques have limited levers to support margins.
Consensus is that the group will not work in the current rate backdrop, and estimates need to rebase lower.

earnings_insights: S&P 500 Q3 consensus (estimate, not yet reported): revenue growth 12.4%, EPS growth 29.6%, margin 15.0%. Q2 actuals for reference: revenue growth 15.6%, EPS growth 52.3%, margin 17%.
Micron reported year/year EPS growth of 1,003% roughly two weeks ago, beat consensus EPS, and guided slightly light. The stock has fallen since.
Big banks JPMorgan, Goldman, Wells Fargo and Citi are scheduled to report tomorrow morning (the text says 'second quarter results' but context is Q3).
Goldman's WFC thesis: the 2026 NII target is $50bn (company target, Goldman estimate on track).
Goldman's BAC estimate: 2027E NII growth of about 7.5% YoY, about 1% above consensus 2027E NII.
Goldman's C estimate: ROTCE of about 11.5% in 2026E and 13.2% in 2028E (Goldman forecasts).

macro_indicators.interpretation: Consensus Q3 EPS growth is down from 52.3% in Q2 and highly concentrated in AI infrastructure names.
Consensus revenue growth is below the 15.6% reported for Q2.
Full-year consensus EPS growth, with FY27 expected to slow to 15.8%.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Down from 14% in Q2, showing the boom is fading for the typical company.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Goldman says the index is 2% from its high while breadth is the weakest since the Dot Com Bubble.
JPM says the Consumer sector is trading as though the consumer is in recession.

crypto_views: Goldman asks whether crypto-trading activity is inflecting or the recent pickup is a flash in the pan, for brokers and exchanges.
Goldman asks how companies view tokenization (institutional adoption) and new products such as event contracts and perpetual futures. Exchanges are favored but market structure uncertainty lingers.
risk_factors: Extreme earnings concentration: Micron and Nvidia account for 34% of Q3 index EPS growth, so a miss or guidance disappointment there carries outsized index impact.
Weak breadth and a Tech stumble could trigger a broader correction.
A hyperscaler capex cut, while seen as unlikely in 2026, would end the AI boom's earnings driver.
Higher rates and oil prices weighing on consumer health, credit (multifamily CRE) and capital markets activity.
Rising rates and AOCI impact reduce excess capital, which could cause buyback pauses at regional banks.
Agentic AI disruption to deposits, retail brokers, wealth, insurance and customer acquisition.
vol_and_positioning: Breadth: 57% of SPX members are in a bear market (down 20%+ from highs) per Bloomberg, with declining dispersion.

Hedge fund exposure to US Financials is around 3-year averages after a rebound. US bank L/S ratio fell sharply in large caps and regionals with some rotation into regionals. Consumer finance L/S is near 2-year lows. Insurance L/S rose QoQ.

Desk positioning scorecard notes: BAC saw a significant sentiment change at the mid-quarter conference, SCHW is a battleground with vocal bulls and bears, TRV is debated with long-only leaning bullish and hedge funds bearish, PGR has divergent views on agentic AI.
In 4 of the last 6 reporting periods the 1-day reaction to beats was below historical median, and misses were punished more heavily.
geopolitical: Iran war oil shock is lifting earnings at Exxon, Chevron and Marathon Petroleum and raising input costs and consumer pressure elsewhere.
cross_bank_references: Article combines Goldman's bank/financials preview with JPMorgan's Market Intel note on S&P 500 earnings watch items.

tension_points.bull_case: Consensus expects 29.6% Q3 S&P 500 EPS growth with all 11 sectors growing, driven by AI infrastructure. JPM sees a hyperscaler capex cut as highly unlikely in 2026.
tension_points.bear_case: Micron and Nvidia account for 34% of growth, the median stock grows only 9%, margin estimates are being cut, and Micron fell after a strong beat, suggesting perfection is priced in.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A capex cut or reduced shareholder distributions from one or more hyperscalers, or a miss or guidance whiff from a top contributor such as Micron or Nvidia.

tension_points.bull_case: Goldman expects asset growth and fixed-rate asset repricing to outweigh higher deposit costs, supporting WFC's $50bn NII target and BAC's NII upside.
tension_points.bear_case: Rising deposit costs amid competition, AOCI pressure on capital, a possible capital markets slowdown after strong 2Q26, and early credit stress in multifamily CRE.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Banks guiding NII or NIM lower or announcing buyback pauses on the Q3 prints, or visible stress in multifamily CRE.
